title: Install or recover Weaver
summary: Install the Weaver CLI and provider under owned maintenance and configure its Annals reader without authoring a document.
use_when: Install the Weaver CLI and provider under owned maintenance and configure its Annals reader without authoring a document.
do_not_use_when: Publication, email, automatic scheduling, source mutation, factual certification, or restoration of the retired Weaver workflow is wanted.
outcome: Install the Weaver CLI and provider under owned maintenance and configure its Annals reader without authoring a document.
effects: Install selects immutable program and provider bytes, initializes supported Weaver SQLite state, stores reading configuration, and acquires and releases run-owned admission holds. It creates no narrative, model job, email, or schedule.
authority: Weaver owns authored Markdown, exact authoring requests, one pending mailbox reply per document, observed execution outcomes, reading configuration, and deployment admission.

Annals owns accepted source documents. Krisis owns decision identification. Nucleus owns execution, authentication, and its retained history. The agent owns editorial interpretation under the user direction.
success: Installed program/provider selection, product initialization/configuration, and release of run-owned holds establish completed setup. Installation does not establish operational readiness.
failure_and_recovery: Resume an uncertain invocation using the identical saved request and job ID. Terminal jobs receive no automatic replacement. Saved documents survive later runtime failure. Deployment recovery uses the coordinator and preserves unproved holds.
privacy: Requests, documents, and pending tool replies are private. Nucleus may retain full source reads. Weaver clears acknowledged replies and keeps documents and invocation records without automatic pruning.

CLI usage recording requires a nonempty CODEX_THREAD_ID. Chancery records command identity, time, and thread ID in its private journal. Arguments, output, outcomes, and internal product calls are excluded. Recording errors do not change command results.
does_not_authorize: Source mutation, remote disclosure, publication, email, state deletion, automatic retry, or effects outside the user-approved endpoint.

consumers.statement: The current local user and authorized Cell agents follow this procedure within the agreed change or maintenance endpoint.

preconditions.statement: Authorized installation or configuration, compatible Annals and Nucleus releases, an existing decisions library, and attributable product-owned selectors. First installation requires annals_config settings.

Prompt preparation requires initialized private Bazaar state and a complete cell.prompts.weaver selection. The default database is ~/.local/share/bazaar/bazaar.sqlite3; callers accept an absolute CELL_BAZAAR_DATABASE override. Reads fail without creating state or using embedded fallback text.

New authoring requires initialized Bazaar state and complete cell.prompts.weaver selection. Import the reviewed migration seed before deployment and preserve its historical selection/text versions; deployment does not supply missing contents.

inputs.statement: The deployment uses a committed local-main candidate. The only setup setting is annals_config, an absolute existing decisions-library config. Init also accepts an absolute annals_binary. Hold and release take exact owner IDs.

outputs.statement: The procedure selects programs and provider, configures the Annals reader, initializes state as required, and releases only its own maintenance hold.

data_semantics.statement: Installation success means local program/provider selection and configuration. It performs no artifact-integrity, state-integrity, or dependency-readiness checks and creates no narrative or email.

identity_and_units.statement: Source commit and retained manager job identities select the delivery. Exact run IDs own maintenance holds. These are separate from authoring document/job identities.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Installer inspection describes release metadata. Doctor and other diagnostics remain separate; installation and catalog presence do not establish live readiness.
No end-to-end delivery, source-read or authoring completion latency is promised.

access.statement: Use the current-user CLI, registered Semantics reader, installed manager, and maintained Cell deployment coordinator. Keep configuration, backups, sources, and runtime records private.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: The coordinator holds and drains Weaver, selects program/provider bytes, invokes product initialization, then releases its own hold. Ordinary initializer rules remain unchanged. Recovery follows the retained transaction.

operational_limits.statement: Readiness probes create no model jobs or synthetic narratives. The procedure preserves private state, owned holds, exact authoring recovery and source authority.
No throughput, retention horizon, future model availability, or automatic authoring retry objective is declared.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Preserve existing public command routes, schema 1, historical exact requests, immutable tool identities and matched program/provider selection. The owned features declare their detailed compatibility rules.
No future compatibility lifetime or deprecation interval is promised.

reliances.statement: The installed CI manager owns serial integration, validation, bounded repair, exact-source deployment and the deterministic outcome email.
The Cell coordinator owns manual deployment selection and interrupted transaction recovery; no dedicated installed Chancery contract covers the coordinator.

session_surfaces: Weaver current-user CLI and private configuration
Cell source tree and installed CI manager
Cell deployment coordinator and product-owned installation evidence
steps: Select the authorized manager delivery or separate validated manual deployment route.
Check explicit Annals reading configuration, compatible providers, supported state and complete Bazaar prompt selection.
Prepare private first-installation settings and preview the coordinator plan.
Use the coordinator to hold, drain, select and configure matched program/provider bytes.
Inspect release metadata and register command inventory. Use doctor separately when live diagnostics are needed.
For attended backup, own a hold, settle exact work, prove drain, save consistent private state, verify and release only that hold.
Use retained coordinator transaction recovery after an interrupted deployment; preserve any unproved hold.
checkpoints: First installation identifies an existing identity-bound Annals decisions config and only supported settings.
Complete drain and exact candidate identity precede installation or state copy.
Database, source and Nucleus checks create no model job or narrative.
The installed overview, focused feature pages and resolve closure describe the matched release.
The retained delivery outcome and release of only the run-owned holds prove the requested endpoint.
adaptation: Reuse stored reading configuration on later deployments unless a deliberate setting changes it.
Use ordinary doctor admission while unheld; while held require the deployment ID to match Weaver's sole hold.
Settle retained assignments with exact resume; cancel only a named Nucleus job the authorized operation intends to abandon.
Before candidate publication retain the prior selection; after publication follow the recorded forward recovery with supported state.
stop_when: State is unsupported or missing outside an authorized initialization.
Dependency inventory or readiness is unavailable, drain is unknown, or another hold prevents the required proof.
A selector is foreign, candidate bytes changed, or the plan exceeds the authorized scope.
Recovery cannot establish the exact coherent installation and its ownership.
